greeting: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen. May the grace and peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, who gathers the little ones into his arms, be with you all.
penitential:
Lord, you are the refuge of the brokenhearted; Lord, have mercy.
Christ, you are the light that shines in our darkness; Christ, have mercy.
Lord, you are the resurrection and the life; Lord, have mercy.
psalm_response: Incline your ear to me and hear my word.
homily:
We often think of our lives as a carefully constructed flight plan. We map out the waypoints, we calculate the fuel, and we trust that if we follow the coordinates—if we are good, if we are smart, if we are careful—we will reach the destination we have envisioned. We look at our children, like Benjamin, and we see a flight plan that is so full of promise, so rich with the potential for altitude and horizon. We see the brilliant mind, the curiosity that reaches toward the clouds, and the gentle heart that navigates the turbulence of life with grace. And then, the flight path changes. The weather shifts in ways we did not choose and could not have predicted. We find ourselves in a place we never intended to land, staring at a silence that feels like a question without an answer.

In the first reading today, we encounter Job. He is a man who had everything—a life built on the bedrock of faith and family—and in a single, terrifying sequence of events, he loses it all. The messengers come one after another, each bringing news of ruin: the livestock taken, the servants slain, the children lost to the wind. It is a scene of utter, devastating loss. And what does Job do? He tears his cloak, he cuts his hair, and he falls to the ground. He does not offer a theological explanation. He does not try to justify the ways of God. He simply speaks the raw, honest truth of his humanity: 'Naked I came forth from my mother's womb, and naked shall I go back again. The LORD gave and the LORD has taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD!'

There is a profound, aching honesty in those words. Job is not being stoic; he is being real. He is naming the reality of the loss while simultaneously anchoring himself in the reality of God. He is teaching us that faith is not the absence of grief, but the ability to hold onto the hand of God while the ground beneath us is shaking. He reminds us that our lives are not our own to possess; they are gifts entrusted to us for a time, and the Giver remains the Giver even when the gift is returned to the source of all light.

Alan and Thao, I know that for these past three months, your hearts have been living in the space between that 'giving' and that 'taking.' You look at the photos—perhaps that one of Ben and Ryan sitting in the church, with the stained glass casting its warm, colored light around them—and you feel the weight of the silence. You remember the way Ben would giggle when he talked about 'con chim airlines,' his dream of taking to the skies. You remember the way he would look at you with that quiet, steady love. And you wonder how to reconcile that vibrant, brilliant spirit with the quiet of his absence. You are doing the holy work of Job. You are mourning, you are grieving, and yet you are still blessing the name of the Lord. That is not a small thing. That is the greatest act of love a parent can offer.

I want to address something that often sits in the shadows of a heart, especially when we have walked the road you are walking. There is a temptation, in the quiet of the night, to look back at the past and wonder if you missed a sign, or if you could have done more. I want to lift that stone from your hearts today. Illness is never a punishment, and it is never the fault of those who loved and cared for the one who suffered. God does not send these sorrows, and He does not hold you responsible for the mysteries of life that are beyond human control. You were the parents Benjamin needed. You were the family he cherished. You did not miss anything. You are not being accused by God, and you must not accuse yourselves. Let that stone fall. You are free to grieve, you are free to miss him, but you are not required to carry the burden of 'what if.' That is a weight that belongs to the dust, and Christ has already stepped into the future to welcome Benjamin home. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him.

In the Gospel today, the disciples are arguing about who among them is the greatest. They are caught up in the vanity of the world, trying to measure their worth by the standards of human achievement. And what does Jesus do? He does not lecture them. He does not offer a complex philosophical argument. He takes a child and places it by his side. He shows them that the greatness of the Kingdom is not found in the power we wield or the logic we master, but in the vulnerability we embrace. 'Whoever receives this child in my name receives me,' he says. 

Benjamin was that child. He was a boy who possessed a brilliant, analytical mind—he could code, he could understand the complexities of cloud infrastructure, he could dream of airlines—but he was also a boy who knew the value of a simple, gentle heart. Think of that moment when he offered his entire piggy bank to help his uncle. He didn't break it, he didn't empty it, he didn't make a show of it. He simply offered. He was a boy who understood that the true currency of the Kingdom is not gold or achievement, but the willingness to give of oneself. He was a boy who lived the truth that Jesus spoke: that the least among us is the greatest.

Ryan, my dear brother, you are the one who knows the rhythm of Ben’s heart better than anyone. You are the one who saw the 'con chim airlines' dreams, who heard the giggles, who shared the everyday life of being a brother. When you feel the loneliness, remember that you are not just a brother who is left behind. You are a brother who is walking forward with his heart inside your own. You are the one who keeps his curiosity alive. Keep being the boy who knows that love is not a thing you lose, but a thing you carry. When you look at the world, when you build, when you create, you are carrying his light into the future. You are the guardian of his memory, and you are the one who is showing the world what it looks like to love a brother with an eternal love.

There is a beautiful, piercing invitation in the Psalm: 'Incline your ear to me and hear my word.' It is a prayer for connection. It is a request for God to draw near to us in our distress. And the promise of the Psalm is that He does. He is the savior of those who flee to Him for refuge. Benjamin has found that refuge. He is at the Banquet of Heaven, resting in the light of Christ, where there is no more pain, no more struggle, and no more silence. He is watching over you with that same sweet, gentle smile, that same quiet, steady love. He is not far away. He is as close as the next breath, as close as the memory that warms your heart, as close as the love you continue to share in his name.

Think of the 'Well of Love' in Vietnam, that clean, life-sustaining water flowing in Ben’s name. It is a perfect image of his life. It is not a closed system; it is a source of life that keeps giving. His kindness, his empathy—the way he wanted to help his uncle, the way he loved his family—that love is still flowing. It is still quenching the thirst of the poor. It is still bringing hope to the weary. His life was a gift that continues to unfold. You are the stewards of that gift. Every act of kindness you do, every time you choose to love instead of despair, you are keeping his spirit alive and flowing into the world. You are the ones who are showing us what it looks like to be faithful in the middle of the mystery.

So, what do you carry out the door today? It is a simple thing, but a profound one. When the world feels like it is just a cycle of vanity, when the silence feels too loud, do not look for answers in the 'why.' Look for the presence in the 'Who.' Whisper his name, and then whisper the name of Jesus. Let those two names be your anchor. You are a family that is being held. You are a family that is being led. You are not just passing through the days; you are moving toward a reunion that is as certain as the rising sun.

Take this with you: you are never walking alone. You have a brother in heaven who is cheering for you, who is praying for you, and who is waiting for you at the end of the flight. Live for him, yes—but live for the One who gave him to you, and who has now called him home. Keep the 'Well of Love' flowing. Keep the kindness moving. Keep the dream alive. And when the evening comes, and you feel the weight of the day, remember the words of the Psalm: 'Incline your ear to me and hear my word.' That ear is always inclined toward you. That heart is always open to you. You are loved without limit, and you are being held by the same hands that hold him. And one day, in the fullness of time, you will see that smile again, and the flight will be complete. Amen.
standing_petitions: For our beloved Ben and all who have gone before us, that they may rest in the eternal light and peace of Christ.
For all families who carry the heavy cross of grief, that they may be consoled by the promise of the Resurrection and held in the arms of God's mercy.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you; may He let His face shine upon you and be gracious to you; may He look upon you with kindness and give you His peace. In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text:
One day, when the angels of God came to present themselves before the LORD,
Satan also came among them.
And the LORD said to Satan, "Whence do you come?"
Then Satan answered the LORD and said,
"From roaming the earth and patrolling it." 
And the LORD said to Satan, "Have you noticed my servant Job,
and that there is no one on earth like him,
blameless and upright, fearing God and avoiding evil?"
But Satan answered the LORD and said,
"Is it for nothing that Job is God-fearing?
Have you not surrounded him and his family
and all that he has with your protection?
You have blessed the work of his hands,
and his livestock are spread over the land.
But now put forth your hand and touch anything that he has,
and surely he will blaspheme you to your face."
And the LORD said to Satan,
"Behold, all that he has is in your power;
only do not lay a hand upon his person."
So Satan went forth from the presence of the LORD.

And so one day, while his sons and his daughters
were eating and drinking wine
in the house of their eldest brother,
a messenger came to Job and said,
"The oxen were ploughing and the asses grazing beside them,
and the Sabeans carried them off in a raid.
They put the herdsmen to the sword,
and I alone have escaped to tell you."
While he was yet speaking, another came and said,
"Lightning has fallen from heaven
and struck the sheep and their shepherds and consumed them;
and I alone have escaped to tell you."
While he was yet speaking, another messenger came and said,
"The Chaldeans formed three columns,
seized the camels, carried them off,
and put those tending them to the sword,
and I alone have escaped to tell you."
While he was yet speaking, another came and said,
"Your sons and daughters were eating and drinking wine
in the house of their eldest brother,
when suddenly a great wind came across the desert
and smote the four corners of the house.
It fell upon the young people and they are dead;
and I alone have escaped to tell you."
Then Job began to tear his cloak and cut off his hair.
He cast himself prostrate upon the ground, and said,

"Naked I came forth from my mother's womb,
and naked shall I go back again.
The LORD gave and the LORD has taken away;
blessed be the name of the LORD!"

In all this Job did not sin,
nor did he say anything disrespectful of God.

readings.label: Responsorial Psalm
readings.text:
R. (6) Incline your ear to me and hear my word.
Hear, O LORD, a just suit;
attend to my outcry;
hearken to my prayer from lips without deceit.
R. Incline your ear to me and hear my word.
From you let my judgment come;
your eyes behold what is right.
Though you test my heart, searching it in the night,
though you try me with fire, you shall find no malice in me.
R. Incline your ear to me and hear my word.
I call upon you, for you will answer me, O God; 
incline your ear to me; hear my word.
Show your wondrous mercies,
O savior of those who flee
from their foes to refuge at your right hand.
R. Incline your ear to me and hear my word.

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text:
An argument arose among the disciples
about which of them was the greatest. 
Jesus realized the intention of their hearts and took a child
and placed it by his side and said to them,
"Whoever receives this child in my name receives me,
and whoever receives me receives the one who sent me.
For the one who is least among all of you
is the one who is the greatest."

Then John said in reply, 
"Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name 
and we tried to prevent him
because he does not follow in our company."
Jesus said to him, 
"Do not prevent him, for whoever is not against you is for you."

day: Monday of the Twenty-sixth Week in Ordinary Time

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Today marks 100 days without you. Miss you a whole a lot Ben. Feel free to visit any time! See you around buddy! Love you!

Ben ơi, nay anh M đi xử lý hồ sơ ở Cam Ranh, đi ngang qua Cam Ranh Airport. Rồi cuộc nói chuyện về máy bay của Ben lại ùa về, nhớ nhiều kỷ niệm về Ben lắm ( anh M sẽ giữ kín kakaka). Quỷ nhỏ, tự nhiên nghĩ về mày buồn dễ sợ. Hãy đi đến những nơi mà Ben muốn nha và đừng quên là luôn nhớ về gia đình mình nhé, thương em trai nhiều. Giá như !!!!!!!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: What happened my son? It's been 3 months since you left us. Missing you so much my whole body aches. Mom cries every day now... What are we going to do now Ben?  Please pray for us.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben,

Rafael Rizzo and his little brother Ben really need your help right now. Please bless them with good health and give them the strength to get through this together. Please watch over Brandon and Flor's health, too.

I miss you a whole bunch. I know you're up in heaven watching over all of us. Whenever you're able to, stop by to visit, yeah? I love you and miss you so much!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text:
Hey Ben - Miss you a whole bunch. Crying all day yesterday, i hope today will be better. Please guide our family through this grief... There's a 14 year old boy that just left earth on August 12... His name is Phero Aden Vo - look for him, maybe you guys can be friends...

Please pray for me and mom to have good health and strength.

I love and miss you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben, Trustin visited you today and left you a few airplane cards—we're putting them in your room for you. Please pray for Trustin and his family to stay healthy and strong. Be a guardian angel to Trustin and Ryan as they go through school, and help guide their steps through every year to come.

Ben ơi, Làm cả ngày tới tối, đến lúc chuẩn bị đi ngủ thì nằm một lúc lại nhớ Ben, nhớ mấy chuyện hai anh em từng nói với nhau. Nghĩ tới em, anh thấy buồn nhiều lắm. Ben hãy luôn theo dõi và cầu nguyện cho ba mẹ và Ryan nhé, nước mắt chảy ngược nó khủng khiếp hơn chảy xuôi đó Ben.

Ben ơi, ba nhớ con nhiều quá.

Mommy cũng vậy. Hơn hai tháng rồi mà ba má vẫn khóc mỗi ngày.

Con giúp ba má vượt qua nha, để lo cho em
